strategy.summary: Reproduce cvxpy#3247: wrong gradient returned by MatrixFrac._grad for matrix X with p>1 columns, caused by using DX.T.ravel(order='F') (equivalent to row-major) instead of DX.ravel(order='F'. Fail the added gradient test on buggy commit b5a20484ff95; pass on the fixed revision containing the transpose removal.

build_commands: # Install cvxpy from the target revision (editable preferred)
pinned_because: # Numerical gradient check is sensitive; keep declared minimums from README for consistent solver/atom behavior

strategy.reproducing_test: In cvxpy/tests/test_grad.py, ensure the MultiVarAtomConfig entry named "matrix_frac_matrix_x" is present, i.e., it tests cp.matrix_frac(x, P) with x shape (3,2) (p>1) and P PSD shape (3,3). The test harness performs a finite-difference gradient check and asserts gradients match.
strategy.success_criterion: On buggy revision b5a20484ff95, the finite-difference gradient check for the "matrix_frac_matrix_x" configuration fails because Atom.grad(MatrixFrac) uses the wrong vectorization order (transpose before ravel), producing silently incorrect gradients when X has more than one column (shape (3,2)). On the fixed revision, the same gradient check passes because the gradient w.r.t. X is vectorized with DX.ravel(order='F') (transpose removed), aligning with CVXPY’s column-major convention.
strategy.numerical_probe: Trigger condition: call Atom.grad/MatrixFrac._grad via the test’s gradient-check harness on cp.matrix_frac(X,P) where X has shape (3,2). The buggy code path uses `DX.T.ravel(order='F')` instead of `DX.ravel(order='F')`, which flips vectorization order and makes the gradient mismatch with the finite-difference approximation.

input_output_examples.input: X is a matrix with more than one column: X has shape (3,2); P is PSD with shape (3,3); operation is cp.matrix_frac(X, P) and the test exercises the gradient w.r.t. X via Atom.grad(MatrixFrac).
input_output_examples.buggy_output: The gradient values produced by Atom.grad for MatrixFrac are silently wrong when p>1; finite-difference comparison reports max error up to ~0.97 (catastrophic).
input_output_examples.expected_output: With transpose removed, gradients match finite-difference with max error ~1.85e-08.

risks: This reproduces only when the gradient check exercises MatrixFrac._grad for X with p>1 (multi-column). If your reproduction accidentally uses X with one column, the transpose bug is masked.

If the test harness depends on a particular backend/differentiation mode, ensure you are running the project’s own test_grad.py exactly as in the diff; the numeric mismatch must be caught by the gradient-check assertion.

If using a different Python/OS or different dependency versions than the stated minima, the finite-difference gradient check might have different tolerances; use the documented min versions from the README constraints to maximize transition fidelity.

If the fixed behavior is only present in a later revision than the one you check out, the test will still fail; you must compare buggy commit b5a20484ff95 vs the corresponding fixed commit from PR#3247 (the one containing the DX transpose removal).

oracle.reference_source: The PR description states finite-difference gradient max error was ~0.97 before the fix and ~1.85e-08 after removing `.T` (vectorizing with DX.ravel(order='F')).
oracle.why: The provided evidence does not include the exact assertion tolerance used in cvxpy/tests/test_grad.py; the success criterion is the pass/fail transition of that existing gradient-check test.

strategy.fails_on_buggy: The test’s finite-difference gradient comparison for MultiVarAtomConfig("matrix_frac_matrix_x") fails because MatrixFrac._grad returns gradients with incorrect vectorization order for X with shape (3,2) (p>1).
strategy.passes_on_fixed: The test passes because MatrixFrac._grad vectorizes DX with column-major order using `DX.ravel(order='F')` (removing the incorrect transpose).
